top_stories.headline: Republicans Hold the Lead in Florida's Governor and Senate Races, Poll Finds
top_stories.deck: The GOP is ahead in both statewide contests a month before the midterms, though Hispanic voters appear to be drifting from the party.
top_stories.body:
A new NBC News poll shows Republicans leading Florida's two marquee midterm races, with about a month to go before voters head to the polls in November.

In the race for governor, Republican Byron Donalds leads Democrat David Jolly, while in the Senate race Republican Sen. Ashley Moody leads Democrat Angie Nixon. An NBC6/Telemundo/Mason-Dixon survey of likely voters put Donalds ahead 48% to 41% and Moody ahead 50% to 40%, margins that fall outside the poll's 4-point margin of error.

The survey also suggests Hispanic voters, who shifted toward Republicans in 2024, are moving away from the party and President Trump — a warning sign for the GOP in a state where Latino voters have become a decisive bloc.

Other recent polls show a wider spread of results, from double-digit Republican leads to essentially tied races, underscoring that Florida's electorate is far from settled. Still, the GOP sits in a strong position in a state that has been trending redder for a decade, and with control of Congress on the line, Florida's outcome could set the tone nationally.

top_stories.headline: Vance Acknowledges Americans' Economic Pain as Trump Paints a Rosier Picture
top_stories.deck: The vice president urges patience on prices while the president insists the economy is strong — a split-screen moment weeks before the midterms.
top_stories.body:
With midterm elections just weeks away, the White House is delivering two different messages on the economy. President Donald Trump has painted a bright picture of his record, pointing to stock market gains and falling gas prices, while Vice President JD Vance has openly acknowledged that many Americans are still struggling.

Speaking at a Breitbart News event, Vance said the administration hears voters' frustration over everyday costs like groceries, and urged the country to be patient as its economic policies take hold. His tone marks a noticeable contrast with Trump's recent insistence that affordability concerns are exaggerated.

The split messaging comes as high prices remain the top concern for voters. Economists have warned that inflation pressures continue, particularly for goods affected by tariffs, and that the benefits of the administration's policies have yet to reach most households.

With control of Congress on the line in November, how voters judge the economy is likely to be the deciding factor — and the administration is now weighing additional steps, including tariff rollbacks and relief checks, to answer the frustration.

top_stories.headline: Tropical Storm Isaias Poised to Become a Hurricane Before Gulf Coast Landfall
top_stories.deck: Forecasters expect the storm to strengthen rapidly and strike the northern Gulf Coast late Friday.
top_stories.body:
Tropical Storm Isaias has formed in the Gulf and is expected to become a hurricane by Thursday before approaching the northern Gulf Coast on Friday, according to forecasters.

The storm is packing winds of about 40 miles per hour and is forecast to intensify quickly as it crosses warm Gulf waters, possibly reaching at least Category 2 strength before making landfall. Models show it could come ashore anywhere from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle late Friday or early Saturday, with much of the impact falling along and east of its path.

Isaias would become the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season and the ninth named storm. Forecasters warn of storm surge, damaging winds, heavy rainfall of up to several inches, and possible tornadoes across the Gulf Coast states, with flooding rain spreading inland over the Southeast through the weekend.

Hurricane watches were expected to be issued Wednesday as residents along the northern Gulf Coast braced for a possible weekend landfall.

top_stories.headline: Nobel Chemistry Prize Honors Scientists Who Solved a Molecular Mirror Mystery
top_stories.deck: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai cracked how chemistry chooses between mirror-image molecules — work with big implications for medicine.
top_stories.body:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in chemistry has been awarded to French chemist Henri B. Kagan and Japanese chemist Kenso Soai for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis, the prize committee announced Wednesday.

Their work answers a long-standing puzzle: many molecules, including amino acids, exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, yet living organisms use only one. Kagan and Soai discovered how chemical reactions can amplify a tiny imbalance until one mirror form dominates — making it far easier to build complex molecules in a single, pure form.

The discovery has practical reach well beyond the lab. Producing single-form molecules with less waste and lower cost matters for medicines, where the wrong mirror image can be useless or even harmful.

The two laureates will share 12 million Swedish kronor in prize money, continuing a week of Nobel announcements that has already honored advances in medicine and physics.

top_stories.headline: Yamamoto Dominates as Dodgers Move One Win From the NLCS
top_stories.deck: The ace struck out 10 over seven innings while Hernández and Freeman homered in a 3-1 win over Atlanta.
top_stories.body:
Yoshinobu Yamamoto struck out 10 over seven innings and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday night to take a 2-1 lead in their National League Division Series.

Yamamoto, last year's World Series MVP, dominated the much-anticipated pitching matchup with Atlanta ace Chris Sale, allowing just four hits and one walk while improving to 8-1 in his postseason career. Sale allowed three runs and seven hits in five innings for the Braves.

Kiké Hernández hit a two-run homer and Freddie Freeman added a solo shot in the fourth inning — all the offense the Dodgers would need. Freeman's drive was the 18th postseason home run of his career, tying him for 10th in major league history.

The two-time defending champions can clinch a berth in the NL Championship Series with a win in Game 4 on Wednesday night, taking another step in their bid to become the first National League team to win three consecutive World Series.

top_stories.headline: The New Sticker Shock: Borrowing Money Costs More Than It Has in Years
top_stories.deck: Mortgage rates are at their highest in nearly three years, and car and education loans are climbing too.
top_stories.body:
Americans looking to buy a home or a car are facing a painful new reality: the cost of borrowing has surged to its highest level in almost three years.

Mortgage rates have climbed above 7 percent, up more than a point and a quarter since February, as the Federal Reserve raises interest rates and bond yields surge. On a median-priced home, that jump adds nearly $300 a month to a typical mortgage payment — enough to put a dream move out of reach.

It's not just housing. The cost of loans for cars and higher education is rising as well, piling more financial pressure on consumers who are already dealing with elevated prices across the economy.

Interest rates for mortgages tend to follow bond yields, which have been climbing in recent months. The result is that life's biggest purchases are falling further out of reach for many households, even as some sellers and borrowers simply sit out the market and wait.

top_stories.headline: Meta's Oversight Board to AI Companies: Don't Grade Your Own Homework
top_stories.deck: The board that reviews Meta's content decisions says AI safety watchdogs need real independence — and real power.
top_stories.body:
Members of Meta's Oversight Board have a warning for artificial intelligence companies racing to build their own safety committees: make them genuinely independent, or don't bother.

In an open letter, the board called for AI governance bodies that operate separately from the companies they oversee, with their own budgets, access to nonpublic information, and the authority to launch investigations and require changes. Effective oversight, they said, should rest on public reasoning and international human rights standards, with experts in cybersecurity, privacy, and child safety at the table.

The advice draws on six years of overseeing content decisions at Meta, during which the board issued 273 decisions and 364 recommendations. The board acknowledged that focusing on a single company was a limitation, and urged AI companies to build shared, industrywide oversight rather than siloed committees.

The message lands as tech leaders and policymakers debate how to keep fast-moving AI systems safe — a debate that has grown louder as powerful models reach hundreds of millions of users worldwide.

briefs.headline: ABC Asks Court to Block Early Review of Its Broadcast Licenses
briefs.deck: An ABC lawyer urged a federal judge to stop what he called an unusual early review of the network's licenses, arguing the looming threat is already chilling editorial decisions weeks before the midterms.

briefs.headline: GOP Senators Warn Trump Has Fumbled the Immigration Issue
briefs.deck: Republican senators say deportation policy, once a clear advantage, has become a growing liability — warning it is hurting GOP candidates with suburban voters ahead of the midterms.

briefs.headline: Kenya Confirms Its First Ebola Case and Death
briefs.deck: A Kenyan citizen who had been living in Congo returned to Nairobi over the weekend, becoming the country's first confirmed Ebola case and first death in the fast-moving outbreak.

briefs.headline: U.S. Troops in Okinawa Face Curfew and Alcohol Ban After Murder Charge
briefs.deck: American forces on Okinawa were barred from drinking alcohol for 48 hours and placed under a 30-day curfew after a Marine was charged with the murder of a local woman.

briefs.headline: Padres Stay Alive in NLDS With Game 3 Win Over Brewers
briefs.deck: A tiebreaking homer from Jake Cronenworth and two relief innings from Game 1 starter Michael King lifted San Diego to a 4-3 win, forcing a Game 4 in Milwaukee.

briefs.headline: Gauff Takes First Career Loss to Mertens, Calls Online Abuse 'Draining'
briefs.deck: Coco Gauff fell to Elise Mertens for the first time in six meetings, then said the abusive comments she received during the China Open had taken a toll.

briefs.headline: Who Will Win the Nobel Prize in Economics? The Betting Markets Have Guesses
briefs.deck: With the prize set to be announced, NPR's Planet Money explores the potential winners and the big ideas that could earn economics' biggest prize.

briefs.headline: Study Names the 15 U.S. Cities Where Groceries Cost Americans the Most
briefs.deck: Inflation has cooled from its pandemic peaks, but grocery prices haven't come down — a painful trend that hits some U.S. cities especially hard, researchers say.

briefs.headline: Death Row Inmate Awake and Speaking After Failed Execution, Lawyers Say
briefs.deck: Christa Pike is communicating in a basic way after her execution failed, according to a medical expert advising her legal team.

briefs.headline: U.S. Moves Long-Range Bombers From U.K. Base Over Possible Iranian Threat
briefs.deck: Washington repositioned the bombers amid rising tensions, while Israelis are learning their prime minister may have been warned before the October 7 attacks.
